text: Under your feet here, a fire has burned for 64 years.
Population? Five.
So why did nobody stop it?
Rewind to 1962.
Centralia, Pennsylvania.
A coal town of about 1,400 people.
The story goes the town burned its trash in an old mining pit,
but that pit sat on old coal mines and the fire got in.
Ooh, coal for me?
So they dug, they flushed.
about $42,000 later, the money ran out. The fire didn't. So how bad could it get?
By 1979, petrol in an underground tank hit 78 degrees Celsius. Is it just me or
the ground? In 1981, the ground opened under a 12-year-old boy, a hole about 45
meters deep. His cousin pulled him out. Now America was watching. Putting the
fire out, one study said about $663 million.
Moving everyone out, 42 million.
Yes, that number again.
So America didn't put out the fire, it put out the town.
Over 500 homes and shops were bought and torn down.
In 2002, even the zip code went.
Today, a handful of people still live there.
Steam still rises through the cracks.
And the twist?
At this rate, it could burn for another 250 years.
Relax, I'm only 64.
